# 元陽子金液集

**ID:** KR5a0239
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0239

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A late-Táng or Five-Dynasties alchemical treatise of fifteen folios, preserved in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 0238 / CT 238 = TC 237), 洞真部 方法類, sharing a Dàozàng fascicle with *[DZ 239 Huándān jīnyè gē zhù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0240)* (a related commentary on a *Huándān jīnyè gē* 還丹金液歌 ascribed to the same Yuányáng zǐ). The text consists of thirty quatrains by Yuányáng zǐ — explicitly invoked as the model in *[DZ 237 Huándān xiǎnmiào tōngyōu jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0238)*'s preface — each followed by an interlinear self-commentary that draws on the canonical alchemical scriptures (the *Yīnfú jīng* 陰符經, the *Cāntóng qì* 參同契, the *Jīnbì jīng* 金碧經, the *Lónghǔ jīng* 龍虎經) and on attributed sayings of figures including Yīn Zhēnjūn 陰真君, Liú Ān 劉安 (淮南王), and Sūn Sīmò 孫思邈. The verses present the elixir process in symbolic terms — *zhēnyīn zhēnyáng* 真陰真陽, *qīnglóng báihǔ* 青龍白虎, *huángyá* 黃芽, *jīnhuá* 金華, *zhū shā* 朱砂 — with constant rejection of vulgar literalising readings that would identify the substances with mundane lead and mercury.

**Abstract**

Schipper, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:787, situates the work in the ninth–tenth century, prior to *[DZ 237 Huándān xiǎnmiào tōngyōu jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0238)* (whose author, Qiánzhēn zǐ, explicitly states that he wrote in imitation of the *Yuányáng zǐ jīnyè jí*) and prior to *[DZ 236 Jīnjīng lùn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0237)* (which absorbs material from DZ 237). Together, DZ 236, DZ 237, and DZ 238 form a tightly interrelated cluster within the Northern-Sòng anthology of *nèidān* poetic exposition. The thirty quatrains and their commentary supply the citation-bedrock for that cluster's theoretical vocabulary. The frontmatter brackets composition accordingly within the late Táng (after 800) and the early Sòng (before 1000), to accommodate a Five-Dynasties (907–960) date as the most likely.
